solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sent elastic strap to go round our uniform pants

indicators.note: the reworked strap goes round the other letters, enclosing them
something elastic stretches out of shape, so the letters of strap are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters it follows are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tale of a stretchy strap fitted round a uniform's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as trousers in the surface but is a second anagram signal; 'Sent' is the past-participle sense of thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent is to be transported with delight, which is what a rapturous person feels.

clue.text: Mounting horse with regulation step gets run over

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pacer is a horse trained to move with a pacing gait

explanation.surface: A jockey climbs onto a horse, and the horse then gets run over.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going back over points already made.

clue.text: One appeals, putting pressure on landlord

parts.note: a landlord leases out property, making him a leaser

explanation.surface: Someone lodges an appeal, leaning on the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeals' looks like a legal appeal, but here it means is attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleaser is someone who charms or gratifies others, one who appeals to them.

clue.text: Cool, practical jars contain rum

indicators.note: to jar is to jolt or shake, so the letters of the words before it are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Plain, sensible jars are found to hold rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jars' looks like a plural noun for containers; it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unromantic is unsentimental and down-to-earth, coolly practical about feelings.

clue.text: Exclusive journalist admitted

parts.note: something of your own belongs to you exclusively
ED, short for editor, is a stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is let in on an exclusive story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' suggests a press scoop next to 'journalist', but it means one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess it, so owned means acknowledged as true.

clue.text: Speedy setter, delightful guy primarily filling in clues

parts.note: super is informal for excellent or delightful

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter of guy is used

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its inside, leaving off the outer letters of clues

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quick crossword setter, a delightful chap, fills in clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter here is a crossword compiler on the surface, but adhesive that sets fast in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Superglue is an adhesive that bonds in seconds, so it is a fast-setting substance.

clue.text: Auditor's folk investigating source of firewood?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what follows is taken as heard

parts.note: cops are police officers, people who investigate crimes

explanation.surface: An auditor's team is probing where some firewood came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking books; here it is simply a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood of trees, cut for poles and logs, so it supplies firewood.

clue.text: Shrewd copper finally got there

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the two words after it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sharp policeman eventually arrived at the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean clever or sharp-witted, especially in American usage, the sense of shrewd.

clue.text: Past master with desire to carry on

parts.note: a past master is an expert, a pro
to long is to desire

explanation.surface: An old hand, wanting to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong is to extend something in time, making it continue further.

clue.text: Completely unknown priest turning up in a German church

indicators.note: the reversed title and unknown sit inside the German word

parts.note: ein is German for a

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest's title
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious cleric is spotted in a German church.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch is an idiom for thoroughly, in every part, so wholly or completely.

clue.text: US car marque not allowed new insignia

indicators.note: not removes the word for allowed from the brand name

parts.note: Chevrolet is an American car brand
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An American car badge is banned and replaced with new insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe worn on a sleeve as a rank badge, a piece of insignia.

clue.text: Staff shielding leaders of experimental team in part of plant

indicators.note: the pole shields the leading letters by surrounding them

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the following words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers protect the heads of a research team inside a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, and 'plant' like a factory; both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: A petiole is the stalk joining a leaf to the stem, a botanical part of a plant.

clue.text: Reactionary Portuguese master turning in back gate in a certain style

indicators.note: turning in means going inside, so the reversed title enters the gate

parts.note: a postern is a rear or side gate

indicators.note: reactionary means acting in reverse, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: Dom is the Portuguese honorific for a master or lord

explanation.surface: A right-wing Portuguese gentleman turns in at the back gate, done in a certain style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reactionary' looks like politics; it signals going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmodern describes a late-20th-century artistic manner, so a work in that particular style.

clue.text: Thin echo emerging from dark wood

indicators.note: the echo letter comes out of the wood, leaving the rest

parts.note: ebony is a hard black wood
E is echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A faint echo comes out of a dark forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' looks like an echoing sound in the woods; it is just the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Bony means so lean that bones show, i.e. very thin.

clue.text: Small band making an impression?

definitions.meaning: on the surface a little musical group; really a ring worn on the finger
on the surface becoming noticed; really pressing a seal into wax

explanation.walkthrough: A small band sounds like a group of musicians getting noticed; it is a finger ring that stamps a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet ring carries an engraved seal that was pressed into wax to authenticate documents.

clue.text: Any short trousers for protective wear

indicators.note: used as a verb, trousers means pockets or takes in
short means cut off at the end, dropping the last letter

parts.note: taken as written
pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Whether any shorts or trousers count as protective clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like a garment, but it is a verb: to trouser is to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment worn over clothes to keep them clean, a form of protective clothing.

clue.text: Graduates brought in to reform old college

indicators.note: the two graduates are put inside the word for reform

parts.note: to alter something is to reform or change it
two MAs, Masters of Arts, are graduates

explanation.surface: Graduates are recruited to reform their former college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the synonym that holds the graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the term for the school or university one attended in the past.

clue.text: Lining up trap: earlier be a victim of one?

indicators.note: the phrase for being caught comes before the trap word

parts.note: to fall in is what a victim of a trap does
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Setting up a trap, someone wonders whether they'd fall for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin is an old word for a snare, nothing to do with the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling in is the military term for soldiers taking their places in a line or rank.

clue.text: Complimentary expression for all-in wrestling?

parts.note: a complimentary ticket is free
style is a manner of expression

explanation.surface: A flattering remark about a no-holds-barred bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complimentary' tempts as praise; it means given free.
explanation.definitionFit: Freestyle wrestling allows holds on the whole body, like all-in wrestling where almost anything goes.

clue.text: Creeper I planted originally in ground close to hedge

indicators.note: the I and the letter are placed inside the word for ground

parts.note: ground grain is milled
taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of planted is used

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close is the end, so the last letter of hedge is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a climbing plant in the soil beside a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeper' looks like a climbing plant in this garden scene; it is a many-legged animal that creeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A millipede is a slow arthropod with many legs that crawls along the ground, a creeping creature.

clue.text: Side with a large following increasingly delayed

indicators.note: the a and large letters follow the word for more delayed

parts.note: later is the comparative of late, so more delayed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team with a big fan base that is running ever later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' tempts as a team; it is an adjective-like noun for a side part.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral relates to the side, so a lateral is a sideways part or pass, a side.

clue.text: Turn of century suits put on for graduation

indicators.note: turn of signals the word for century is turned round

parts.note: a ton is a hundred
clubs and hearts are card suits, C and H

explanation.surface: At the turn of the century, students don suits for their graduation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduation' suggests a ceremony; here it means a mark on a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduation is a marked step on a measuring scale, and a notch is one such mark or step.

clue.text: Stated couple settles for partial head coverings

indicators.note: stated means said aloud, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a couple is two, and settles means pays, as with a bill

explanation.surface: A couple are said to be settling down to wear hairpieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Toupee is pronounced too-pay, hence two pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee is a small hairpiece that covers a bald patch, so only part of the head.

clue.text: US college team's first baseball kit

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The leading baseball equipment for an American college team.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitt is the padded glove a baseball fielder wears, part of the player's gear.

clue.text: Biddable character given a gentle hint

parts.note: taken as written
soft means mild or gentle
a touch is a slight trace or hint, as in a touch of irony

explanation.surface: An obedient person needs only a light nudge.
explanation.walkthrough: A soft touch is someone easily persuaded, especially into lending money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person who is easily talked into things, a pushover.

clue.text: Fake warning from driver about end of parking

indicators.note: about means around, so the warning goes round the letter

parts.note: Fore is the golfer's shout of warning after a drive

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of parking

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorist's bogus warning about parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist next to 'parking'; it is a golfer striking from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge is to make a counterfeit copy, such as a fake signature or banknote.

clue.text: Was repelled by violent death

indicators.note: violent suggests a rough disturbance, so the letters of death are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recoiled at a brutal killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hated something is to have felt strong aversion or loathing for it.

clue.text: Couple without love kiss and curse

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the love letter is removed

parts.note: to couple things is to join them
love is zero in tennis, written O
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A pair, no longer in love, kiss and swear at each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a pair of people; it is a verb, to join.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a spell of bad luck, a hex or curse put on someone.

clue.text: Nervously try fire alarm a lot

indicators.note: nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Anxiously test the fire alarm frequently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire alarm' reads as one noun; 'alarm' joins 'a lot' for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To terrify is to frighten someone very badly, far more than a mild scare.

clue.text: Endeavour to slash regular outlay for clothing

indicators.note: slashing cuts into the rent, letting the endeavour in

parts.note: rent is a regular payment
to aim is to try or endeavour

explanation.surface: Trying to cut regular spending on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash' looks like cutting costs; the aim word cuts into the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or apparel.

clue.text: King going outside city to unwind

indicators.note: the king goes outside the city, enclosing it

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A monarch leaves town to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to rest and let tension go, an idiom for easing off.

clue.text: Vital English engineers in draft heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west is reading right to left
the engineers go inside the draft word

parts.note: a draft is a design or plan
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Crucial English engineers in a design heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means full of energy and lively, so invigorated or energised.
